- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid “overcorrection”.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.17) and price is trending up, model underestimates upside — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–5 days — if sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.17 to -0.5), adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of recent 10–15 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often forecasts a steeper decline — reduce forecast slope by 0.3–0.7% per day to avoid “panic” overreaction.
